top_issues: The legend text for 'Two colours, one rule' is explanatory prose rather than a concise, accessible indicator, forcing elderly or hurried users to parse dense copy to understand balance integrity.
Small secondary labels ('Spendable now $175.00 · can receive $250.75') lack contrast against the dark card background (#12151c) and will fail outdoor or low-vision readability.
The segmented proportional balance bar directly beneath $155.00 is thin (approx 4px tall) and difficult to touch-target or visually separate when green/violet boundaries meet.
fixes: Increase proportional bar thickness from 4px to 8px with rounded caps and high-contrast color dividers.
Convert the 'Two colours, one rule' callout into a persistent two-chip badge row: [Enforceable $40.00] and [Promised $115.00] with icon status.
Raise font size of spendable/receivable capacity from 13px to 15px and boost muted text contrast to at least 4.5:1.

top_issues: The account credit capacity bar under 'H1 hub' has ultra-faint grey labels ('send up to 175.00', 'receive up to 0.50') that blend into the container background.
Recent activity items rely on subtle directional icons with micro timestamps ('05:23') without clear dates, making reconciliation hard across calendar days.
The 'Swap closed' entry displays zero counter-amount or received value, leaving users guessing whether an execution took place or was cancelled.
fixes: Add explicit settled amounts to all activity list rows (e.g. show trade pair and filled amount on 'Swap closed').
Elevate text color of 'send up to / receive up to' capacity numbers from #5a6275 to #9aa3be.
Include relative date grouping headers ('Today', 'Yesterday') above transactions.

top_issues: The recipient hex address ('0x92c2d7c32d...') in the 'To' card is truncated in the middle of a dense 2-line string without an explicit copy button or checksum badge.
The available sending capacity indicator ('Up to 175.00 instantly') is isolated at the top right of the amount card, separated from the actual primary input field.
Fee shown as 'under 0.01 USDC' lacks exactness for micro-auditing and corporate record-keeping.
fixes: Place an interactive copy/paste icon next to the recipient address and format as '0x92c2...cbf0' with an address book contact badge.
Move 'Max spendable: 175.00 USDC' directly beside or below the amount input with a 'MAX' button.
Provide a tooltip or tap state on 'under 0.01 USDC' that reveals the exact 6-decimal fee (e.g. 0.000050 USDC).

top_issues: The route selection cards ('You -> H1 -> H2' vs 'You -> H1 -> H3 -> H2') show raw 6-decimal fractions ('0.000050') without explaining why one would pick a 2-hop route over a 1-hop route.
The primary CTA button 'Pay 25.00 USDC' is pressed against the bottom navigation margin on tall mobile viewports, risking thumb collision.
The small toggle text 'Add a note' has minimal affordance (low contrast purple with tiny chevron).
fixes: Label route cards with human differentiators, e.g., 'Direct / Fastest (0.000050 USDC)' and 'Alternate Hub (0.000075 USDC)'.
Add standard safe-area bottom padding (min 24px) beneath 'Pay 25.00 USDC'.
Increase 'Add a note' click target height to 44px with a subtle pill boundary.

top_issues: The modal sheet dark backdrop completely obscures the preceding context, making it hard to verify what background balances just changed without dismissing.
Proof hash is truncated ('0x00109fe5...6bec') with no visual affordance indicating that tapping copies the full cryptographic proof.
Settlement speed 'in 9 s' in bright green can be misleadingly interpreted as a pending timer rather than elapsed finality.
fixes: Replace 'in 9 s' with 'Settled in 9s' or 'Finality: 9s' with a settled checkmark.
Add a distinct copy icon next to the Proof hash row.
Ensure the bottom sheet dismiss handle and backdrop allow a 10% peek of the updated balance header.

top_issues: Four horizontal buttons at the bottom ('Copy receipt', 'Download', 'Print / PDF', 'Done') compress the tap targets on narrow phone viewports.
'Verified by your runtime' is reassuring to developers but provides zero tangible meaning to everyday consumers like Rosa or Lucas.
The background home screen accounts row is visibly clipped behind the card overlay.
fixes: Stack the primary action ('Done') full width, placing secondary actions ('Copy', 'PDF') in an icon-led toolbar above it.
Change 'Verified by your runtime' to 'Co-signed & cryptographically verified by your device'.
Maintain clean scrim blur behind modal cards.

top_issues: The QR code container dominates the entire viewport, pushing the critical incoming capacity restriction ('25.50 capacity via H1') below the immediate initial glance.
Payer incoming capacity ('25.50 capacity via H1') is easy to miss, meaning a merchant asking for $50 won't immediately know the channel can't receive it.
Amount input is labelled 'Amount · optional' with '0.00' in grey, which can be confused with an already-set amount.
fixes: Highlight channel incoming capacity with an explicit warning badge if requested amount exceeds inbound capacity.
Reduce QR box size by 15% on mobile to allow the amount input and route dropdown to be visible above the keyboard.
Make '0.00' clear placeholder text and autofocus amount input on tap.

top_issues: YOUR ENTITY ID displays a truncated hash ('0xbad0865d...67985a') without a direct 1-tap copy button or share trigger in that specific card.
The explanation text in the share card is verbose ('Send the link or show the code. It opens in any browser...').
The 'Print / PDF' button under the big purple 'Copy payment link' button lacks standard button boundaries or touch feedback.
fixes: Add a dedicated 'Copy ID' button right inside the 'YOUR ENTITY ID' card.
Condense share card description to a single concise line: 'Instant settlement link for any web browser.'
Elevate 'Print / PDF' to a bordered secondary button styled consistently with the 'Copy payment link' CTA.

top_issues: The 'Gross receive' legalistic card contains heavy dense text ('H1 collateral tariff: 0.1 WETH base + 0 WETH gas...') that induces anxiety in non-technical users.
The network badge ('Testnet') looks identical to interactive dropdown pills, confusing environment status with token selection.
The exchange rate calculation is tucked under small table rows ('Limit price: 2,500.5000 USDC per WETH') without a quick inversion toggle (1 WETH = X USDC vs 1 USDC = Y WETH).
fixes: Move the collateral tariff disclaimer behind an info popover or expander, summarizing it as 'Estimated hub fee: <0.01%'.
Add a bidirectional toggle icon on the limit price row to invert rate display.
Style 'Testnet' with an amber subtle tag rather than standard dark interactive card styling.

top_issues: The order book preview at the very bottom shows only 'BOOK' header peeking out, requiring an unintuitive scroll to see market depth.
Numbers in the depth table display 4 decimal places uniformly ('2,508.0000', '30.6000'), crowding mobile width.
Tapping a level text explains 'Tap a level to fill the ticket', but the tap targets in the book are less than 28px tall, causing mis-taps.
fixes: Increase depth row line-height to provide at least 36px touch targets for each book price tier.
Format order book prices with trailing zero dimming to spotlight significant digits.
Provide a sticky bottom drawer pull indicator for the Orderbook.

top_issues: Crucial multi-hop complexity ('Testnet -> H1 -> Tron') is presented with the same visual weight as simple single-hop swaps.
The red warning text 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' at the bottom is cut off on typical phone screens without scrolling.
Zero indication of cross-chain execution time or bridge finality window in the route summary table.
fixes: Add an explicit estimated execution time row (e.g. 'Est. settlement: ~15-30s') for cross-network routes.
Pin the capacity warning directly above the action button with an inline resolution link.
Visually distinguish cross-chain hub route hops with clear network icon badges.

top_issues: The capacity slider ('100% collateral' to '0% collateral') combined with 'Extend credit limit' breaks the mental model of a simple cross-chain swap.
The checkbox 'Add 10% buffer to new credit only (0.0008 WETH)' introduces micro-math that overwhelms retail users.
The button 'Extend credit limit' replaces 'Swap', confusing whether the user is executing a trade or modifying counterparty risk limits.
fixes: Separate risk line adjustments into a pre-flight modal: 'One-time setup: enable H3 incoming capacity' with a single recommended default.
Remove raw 6-digit decimal buffers from checkbox copy, replacing with 'Auto-add buffer for smooth trading'.
Keep the primary CTA text clear: 'Approve limit & Swap'.

top_issues: Action grid has 5 buttons in an asymmetrical 3-on-top, 2-on-bottom layout with uneven visual weight.
Color key legend (green = secured, purple = promised, yellow = you owe, grey = credit room, striped = in flight) has 5 items crammed into small text that is difficult to scan.
Difference between 'Their credit line to you' (0.00) and 'Your credit line to them' (115.50) is counterintuitive and inverted for ordinary bank users.
fixes: Normalize the account actions into an evenly spaced 4-action grid or segmented tab bar.
Simplify the color legend into an interactive tapped breakdown drawer.
Use plain-language credit descriptions: 'You allow H1 to owe up to $115.50' instead of abstract bilateral terminology.

top_issues: Row 'They owe you, uncovered $90.00 Cover it' combines status and actionable link into a cramped line where 'Cover it' is easily clicked accidentally.
'If you dispute, they answer within 1 d' sounds intimidating and leaves ambiguity about what happens during that 1-day lockup.
Status 'Open' in green mimics the settlement/enforceability green, conflating operational state with funds safety.
fixes: Turn 'Cover it' into a distinct pill button with padding to prevent accidental mis-taps.
Change status 'Open' color to a neutral slate blue to preserve green strictly for enforceable funds.
Add an info icon next to '1 d dispute window' explaining the challenge resolution cycle.

top_issues: The modal tabs ('Collateral', 'Credit', 'Add token', 'Dispute') treat 'Dispute' as just another configuration tab instead of an emergency protocol action.
The button 'Dispute this account...' uses an ominous red/brown hue that does not convey standard system danger clearly.
Step 1 states 'the latest page both of you signed goes on-chain with your next batch' without telling the user how much gas or on-chain fee will be consumed.
fixes: Isolate 'Dispute' from everyday management tabs into a dedicated emergency action section with distinct visual warning styling.
Display estimated on-chain gas costs required to execute the dispute transaction.
Use high-contrast warning amber/crimson with a clear confirmation slider or double-tap safeguard.

top_issues: Bottom sheet contents are pushed down, leaving awkward dead space at the top while the crucial final trigger button sits close to screen edge.
The term 'latest page' introduces a third metaphor (pages vs frames vs entries), confusing developers and compliance reviewers.
No preview of the exact state being committed (balance, sequence number, counterparty signature).
fixes: Unify nomenclature: replace 'latest page' with 'latest co-signed frame (#81)'.
Add a small collapsible preview showing the exact frame hash and balances to be submitted on-chain.
Ensure consistent sheet top margin and auto-scroll to reveal the trigger button with 32px bottom clearance.

top_issues: Header summary ('Today · in $140.00 · out $68.58 · 5 movements') wraps awkwardly into 3 tiny lines next to 'Activity'.
Filter pills row is horizontally clipped ('Accou...' is truncated at the right edge without a clear fade indicator).
'Export CSV' is an unadorned text link in a small font, easy to overlook for business owners and auditors.
fixes: Restructure header to place aggregate volume ('+$140.00 / -$68.58') in a clean horizontal metric bar below the title.
Turn 'Export CSV' into an icon-button (download icon + 'CSV') positioned neatly in the top right.
Add a subtle gradient fade mask to the right edge of the horizontal filter pill container.

top_issues: The proof hash '0x00109fe5...346bec' is truncated, which blocks compliance officers from manual inspection without tapping download.
Action buttons 'Copy' and 'Download proof' have identical visual weight, making it unclear which one provides the full cryptographic bundle.
'2 committed entries' row lacks an expand chevron to view the individual entries inside frame #81.
fixes: Make the '2 committed entries' row expandable to reveal sub-transactions inline.
Differentiate actions: make 'Download proof' primary and 'Copy link/summary' secondary outline.
Add a quick verification badge showing both user and hub signature statuses explicitly.

top_issues: The 'Dollars per pixel' slider is an unusual visualization concept that will baffle mainstream users who just want to see their money.
Preset scale pills ('Auto', '$1', '$2', '$5', '$10', '$25', '$100') crowd together and dominate the top of Settings above critical security controls.
Switch toggles ('On-chain wallet', 'Reserve', 'Accounts') describe internal architecture rather than user-centric settings.
fixes: Move the bar scale slider into an 'Advanced Display' sub-menu, keeping Auto as default.
Reorder settings to prioritize Security, Vault, and Connected Hubs before visual scaling.
Clarify toggles as 'Show/hide balance layers on home screen'.

top_issues: 'At this scale' bar chart demo ($100 = 10 px, $1,000 = 100 px, etc.) takes up massive vertical real estate without offering functional settings utility.
'Forget vault' is placed directly next to 'Lock' and 'Reveal recovery phrase', risking catastrophic accidental wallet deletion if tapped carelessly.
Runtime ID hash ('0x27a60f6d...') takes prominent space while offering no interactive debugging utilities on mobile.
fixes: Isolate 'Forget vault' into a distinct red destructive zone at the bottom of the screen with a confirmation prompt.
Replace the static scale reference chart with a compact interactive sample preview.
Add a 1-tap copy icon to the Runtime ID row.

top_issues: The two 3-box matrices for 'FROM' and 'TO' (Wallet, Reserve, Account) look identical, making it easy to invert the transfer direction accidentally.
The visual state of the selected card is indicated only by a subtle blue border outline (#4f6bff), which is easily missed.
Balances inside non-selected cards are static and do not update dynamically to reflect after-transfer projections.
fixes: Introduce an explicit directional arrow badge between FROM and TO containers, and shade non-selected source cards darker.
Add a prominent selected checkmark badge in the corner of active source/target cards.
Show projected destination balance (e.g. '$150.00 -> $175.00') directly inside the target card.

top_issues: Secondary action 'Add to batch' has identical width to 'Sign & send', diluting the primary path for single movements.
The explanatory card 'WHAT HAPPENS' uses academic phrasing ('Reserve to account posts collateral on-chain; the account can then be used instantly').
Recipient entity input ('leave empty for yourself') uses placeholder text that disappears when touched, leaving no persistent label.
fixes: Make 'Sign & send' the prominent primary button and reduce 'Add to batch' to a secondary text action or icon button.
Provide a persistent floating label for 'Recipient entity (optional)'.
Simplify explanation: 'Funds move from Depository into your H1 instant balance'.

top_issues: Top navigation grid has an odd 5th element ('Ownership') centered in a third row, creating an unbalanced layout.
'Where your money stands' summary repeats the home balance data without providing quick links to reallocate or rebalance.
'Needs attention: Nothing waiting on you' is plain text that lacks positive affirmation or status iconography.
fixes: Reorganize the top section into an even 4 or 6 item card grid (add 'Disputes' or 'Routing' as the 6th tile).
Add action buttons next to 'Promised by hubs' to allow 1-tap collateral requests directly from Manage.
Add a green shield icon to 'Nothing waiting on you' to reinforce safety.

top_issues: The note 'Depository may pull 0.00' under each token is cryptographically descriptive but creates user anxiety about unauthorized fund pulls.
The single action button 'Move into reserve' is left-aligned and awkwardly floating inside the card list.
Gas balance ('0.1000 ETH') has no fiat valuation equivalent (~$250.00), leaving users unsure of actual purchasing power.
fixes: Change 'Depository may pull 0.00' to plain 'Approved for reserve: $0.00' with an edit limit button.
Display estimated fiat value beside the Gas balance (e.g. '0.1000 ETH ≈ $250.00').
Make 'Move into reserve' full width at the bottom of the On-Chain Wallet card.

top_issues: The screen features three stacked action buttons with confusing nuances: 'Receive USDC from H1', 'USDC to my on-chain wallet', 'USDC straight into my reserve'.
The capacity buffer configuration occupies the entire upper viewport, pushing the destination buttons out of view.
The permanent credit limit notification ('115.499973 USDC -> 197.449948 USDC') displays unrounded 6-digit micro-numbers.
fixes: Round credit limit updates to 2 decimal places in user-facing dialogs ('115.50 -> 197.45 USDC').
Combine withdrawal destinations into a clean picker instead of 3 nearly identical stacked buttons.
Provide a single 'Confirm Limit & Receive' action.

top_issues: Lend/Borrow toggle is placed below the token selection cards rather than at the top of the interface, violating standard workflow hierarchy.
Term selector buttons ('1 hour', '1 day', '1 month') lack rate indications or market interest estimates.
The selected Hub ('H1 - 3 lanes') does not show its total lending capacity or risk rating.
fixes: Move the Lend / Borrow segment toggle to the very top of the screen.
Display current market benchmark APY directly below each Term selection pill.
Show Hub collateralization ratio and active pool utilization alongside H1.

top_issues: H1 POOL stats at the bottom show '0.00' for Available, Borrowed, and Active principal, giving no indication whether the pool is active or empty.
The rate input shows '100 basis points = 1.00% per term' which creates confusion between annual APY and absolute term interest.
'Offer to the pool' button is active even when amount is 0.00.
fixes: Clarify rate display to show both annualized rate (APR) and term payout in dollars.
Disable 'Offer to the pool' button with disabled styling until a valid non-zero amount is entered.
Add pool health status indicator ('Pool Idle / 0 active liquidity').

top_issues: The definition 'Kind: Self-issued (its id is the hash of its board)' and 'lazy entity' uses internal protocol vernacular unintelligible to business operators.
No interactive button exists to start a board key rotation, add a second signer, or set up multi-sig quorum.
Card 'TAKE CONTROL OF ANOTHER ENTITY' is largely empty and doesn't explain how an operator receives or imports co-signing authority.
fixes: Add an 'Add Key / Setup Multi-sig' action button inside the Board card.
Replace 'lazy entity' with plain terminology: 'Unregistered Local Account (Off-chain identity)'.
Provide an 'Import Invitations / Authority' button in the Take Control card.

top_issues: Hero balance says 'Enforceable right now $40.00' while the Total balance ($130.00) is omitted from the top header, which might cause panic that $90 disappeared.
The 4-level breakdown ('On-chain', 'Reserve', 'Collateral behind what you are owed', 'Promised') is mathematically sound but visually dense.
Signer address ('0xf2435cb2...f9ab06') and Entity ID are truncated with no quick copy icon.
fixes: Display Total Portfolio ($130.00) above Enforceable ($40.00) so users immediately see both total net worth and guaranteed floor.
Add a 1-tap copy icon beside Signer, Entity, and Depository addresses.
Provide a visual slider showing how moving funds into Reserve increases the Enforceable bar.

top_issues: The button 'Save evidence bundle' does not clarify the file format (.json proof bundle) or whether it can be loaded into an independent external viewer.
'Accounts co-signed 1 of 1' and 'Can dispute without asking 1 of 1' look like fractional numbers rather than boolean health guarantees.
'nothing at risk' in bright green in the PER COUNTERPARTY card could be misinterpreted as meaning the $90 hub balance is completely risk-free.
fixes: Change 'Save evidence bundle' to 'Export Signed Dispute Bundle (.json)'.
Rephrase 'nothing at risk' to 'Fully co-signed · proof on file' to avoid giving false assurances about unsecured credit.
Format '1 of 1' counters as status pills: '[✓ 100% Co-signed]'.

overall.verdict: The xln mobile dark interface achieves extraordinary technical depth, bringing formal verification and bilateral credit physics directly to the glass with razor-sharp typography and an uncompromising integrity model. However, it frequently burdens everyday retail personas with raw protocol machinery—such as micro-fractional limits, bilateral credit mathematics, and internal frame semantics—where simple financial confidence is required.
priority_fixes: Replace raw 6-decimal fractions and micro-credit calculations across Swap and Receive with rounded 2-decimal numbers and automated collateral buffers.
Consolidate the 'Two colours, one rule' narrative into persistent, self-explanatory UI chips ([Guaranteed On-Chain] vs [Hub Promise]) with direct 1-tap rebalancing.
Separate the emergency 'Dispute' flow from standard configuration tabs into a dedicated fail-safe screen with explicit on-chain gas estimates and frame snapshots.
Clean up the bottom navigation safe zones and primary CTA button hierarchies, removing secondary actions like 'Add to batch' from default consumer paths.
Provide an expandable full cryptographic audit viewer for proofs, receipts, and co-signed frames with single-tap export for accounting and compliance.

personas.name: Rosa
personas.verdict: The numbers are big and sharp, but there is so much confusing talk about promises, collateral, and hubs that I am scared to touch the wrong thing.
blockers: Cannot easily tell why her balance is split between green and purple bars on 01-home.png without reading dense technical small print.
Cramped address display and missing contact names on 02-pay.png make sending $50 to her grandson feel risky.
Accidental exposure to the raw 'Dispute' tab on 06b-dispute.png causes severe anxiety about irreversible account freezing.

personas.name: Jamal
personas.verdict: I can see my money land instantly, but having to manually learn about depository reserves just to lock in my week's pay is a headache.
blockers: The matrix on 10-move.png (Wallet vs Reserve vs Account) makes transferring his gig earnings to safe long-term holding confusing.
Incoming channel capacity restrictions on 04-receive.png threaten to block incoming tips unless he monitors inbound credit limits.
Activity feed on 01-home-bottom.png groups transfers by cryptic hub hops ('Sent to H2 via H1') instead of customer or platform names.

personas.name: Priya
personas.verdict: Generating the QR code is fast for my counter, but if a busy rush exceeds my inbound hub room, payments will get stuck and closing reconciliation is too fiddly.
blockers: Inbound capacity limit ('25.50 capacity via H1') on 04-receive.png silently caps what customers can pay her until credit is manually extended.
Activity export CSV on 07-activity.png is an easily-missed text link rather than a prominent end-of-day register report.
Receipts on 03-receipt.png hide the individual customer payment note behind sub-menus.

personas.name: Wei
personas.verdict: The bilateral orderbook and exact tick sizing are outstanding, giving me full visibility into my hub exposure and counterparty debt before I size up.
blockers: Order book rows on 05-swap-bottom.png are too vertically cramped for fast one-handed limit order placement on mobile.
Lack of direct inverse pricing toggle (WETH/USDC vs USDC/WETH) on 05-swap.png slows down rapid cross-arbitrage execution.
The 1-day dispute resolution window on 06-account-bottom.png lacks a live on-chain gas fee estimator for immediate unilateral exit.

personas.name: Elena
personas.verdict: Every state transition carries a verifiable co-signed frame and cryptographic proof, providing the cleanest audit trail in the industry if export tools are streamlined.
blockers: Activity proof hashes on 08-activity-detail.png are truncated, preventing visual manual verification against external court filings without downloading the bundle.
CSV export on 07-activity.png does not document whether entries include full counterparty ECDSA signature hashes in the flat export table.
No bulk batch verification screen to validate all 15 signed frames from screen 06-account-bottom.png in one operation.

personas.name: Noah
personas.verdict: The UI models the RJEA state machine with extraordinary fidelity—replicas, frames, credit limits, and depository reserves map directly to the canonical architecture.
blockers: Screen 06b-dispute-bottom.png uses the colloquial word 'page' ('latest page both of you signed') instead of canonical 'frame', momentarily blurring the protocol abstraction.
Screen 14-ownership.png lacks an explicit JSON view of the board schema and quorum threshold rotation payload.
The runtime status on 09-settings-bottom.png shows frame #44 while activity shows frame #81, creating an apparent state synchronization discrepancy.

personas.name: Aisha
personas.verdict: Cross-network payroll is theoretically supported, but having to manually calculate WETH credit buffers and Tron accounts on a weak connection will lead to stuck field payments.
blockers: Cross-network swap on 05b-swap-cross.png abruptly halts with 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' without auto-resolving the channel allocation.
Slider configuration on 05b-swap-cross-bottom.png demands that she understand collateral ratios just to transfer USDT across chains.
No explicit offline queue indicator showing whether signed transactions will safely retry when connection drops in the field.

personas.name: Lucas
personas.verdict: It looks sick and dark like a hacker terminal, but what on earth is an 'Entity ID', 'Depository escrow', or 'collateral tariff' when I just want $10 of ETH?
blockers: Swap screen on 05-swap.png warns about '0.1 WETH base + 0 WETH gas' collateral tariffs, making him think buying $10 of ETH costs hundreds in fees.
No simple 'Buy with Card' or fiat onramp entry point anywhere on 01-home.png.
Settings screen 09-settings.png opens with 'Dollars per pixel' slider instead of profile, notifications, or simple currency selection.

personas.name: Ingrid
personas.verdict: This is the first wallet that treats counterparty credit risk rigorously, allowing me to quantify exact uncollateralized exposure down to the dollar.
blockers: The 'Cover it' shortcut on 06-account-bottom.png does not show the required capital or depository reserve balance before clicking.
Screen 15-sovereignty.png hero section omits the ratio of uncollateralized credit to total assets (e.g. 69.2% Hub Exposure).
Lending screen 13-lend-bottom.png shows zero pool utilization data, making it impossible to evaluate hub creditworthiness for liquidity placement.

personas.name: Omar
personas.verdict: I can see the mechanics of credit lines and dispute windows, but the wallet is strictly consumer-facing and doesn't reveal the hub fee income or operator routing yield.
blockers: Screen 13-lend-bottom.png does not break down the spread earned between hub borrowing tariffs and user lending yields.
No hub operator dashboard exists to monitor aggregate client credit lines, rebalancing triggers, or depository collateral demands.
Dispute screen 06b-dispute.png describes what happens if the hub misbehaves, but not the automated counter-proof submission process from the hub daemon side.
